entities.name: PMID:25098338
observations: Haji et al., 2014, cross-sectional survey of guardians of children with suspected malaria attending health centres in Oromia, Ethiopia; n=830.

Abstract reports children whose guardians suspected covert HIV testing had median presentation delay of 3 versus 2 days (p<0.001); concern associated with higher odds of delay ≥3 days (OR 1.73; abstract renders 95% CI upper limit as 270, likely 2.70).

entities.name: Covert testing delays malaria care
observations: In an Ethiopian cross-sectional sample of 830 guardians, belief that blood was covertly tested for HIV was associated with longer child presentation delay (median 3 vs 2 days, p<0.001) and higher odds of delay ≥3 days (OR 1.73; abstract CI displayed 1.10–270, likely 1.10–2.70). Association is observational, not proof of causation.
